# STRUDEX — Strudel Expander

A browser studio for live-coding music with Strudel (JavaScript). Each track is
one readable `.js` file; the panel is a live view over that code (mixer, timeline,
automation). It is designed to be driven by an AI agent as well as a human.

## Quickstart for an agent

1. Open the site. Close the intro with `window.strudex.closeIntro()`.
2. Read, in order:
   - `/docs/prompt-track.en.md` — the track-generation brief and file standard
   - `/docs/rules.en.md` — style frames and anti-patterns
   - `/docs/pitfalls.en.md` — Strudel gotchas (mandatory)
   - `/docs/references.en.md` — external sources index
3. Study examples under `/tracks/_selected/` (public set) and
   `/tracks/coldwave/03-cold-rooms-v3.js` (full reference: TIMELINE, AUTOMATION,
   `autoCurve`, `tlCurve`, `UI` manifest).
4. Write the track, then apply and start it in one call:
   `window.strudex.setCode(code)`.
5. When the user asks for changes: `const cur = window.strudex.getCode()`,
   edit it, `window.strudex.setCode(edited)` again.

Hard rules: sound must work in stock strudel.cc; mini-notation only through
`m(...)`; automation only via native `autoCurve`/`arrange`; no negative literals
in `slider(...)`.

This is **not SUNO**: you generate code for browser synthesizers, not audio.
Never imitate acoustic instruments (saxophone, flute, violin, trumpet, winds) and
never add vocals or "songs". If the user explicitly asks for those, say plainly
that this is a synth/electronic studio and offer the closest electronic timbre
(Moog-like voice, Rhodes, synth brass). With no explicit request, silently pick
the electronic equivalent — do not announce it. See `/docs/rules.en.md`.

## Stable browser API — `window.strudex`

| Method | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ready()` | Promise; resolves when the engine has booted |
| `closeIntro()` | Close the intro overlay if open |
| `listTracks()` | Promise<string[]> of track paths from `/api/tracks` |
| `loadTrack(path)` | Load and play a track file |
| `newTrack()` | Load the blank starter (`/tracks/_selected/new-track.js`) |
| `getCode()` | Current editor code as a string |
| `setCode(code)` | Replace the editor code, evaluate and play |
| `play()` / `stop()` | Transport |
| `getTrack()` | Currently loaded track path |
| `getStatus()` | Status-line text (errors show up here) |

UI ids if a real click is needed: `#track` (picker), `#newTrack`, `#play`,
`#stop`, `#root` (editor), `#status`, `#help`.

## Track shape

`setcpm(BPM/4)` → optional `samples({...})` → `const UI` (transport/switches) →
`const instruments` (mixer tree of `slider(...)`) → `const TIMELINE` →
`const AUTOMATION` → helper functions (`tlCurve`, `tlOr`, `gateOf`, `autoCurve`,
`autoAt`) → `$:` lanes. See `/docs/prompt-track.en.md` for the full standard and
`/tracks/_selected/new-track.js` for a tiny two-section starter.

## Hosts

- Localhost sees the full library.
- Any other host (the public deployment) lists and serves only
  `/tracks/_selected/`; other track files answer 404.
